title: Mainstay Alternatives for Online and Adult Enrollment
summary: Mainstay alternatives for online and adult enrollment in 2026: six vendors compared on voice, text-to-call, warm transfer and CRM write-back.
body_markdown:
The strongest Mainstay alternatives for online and adult enrollment in 2026 are Element451's Bolt agents, Mongoose, Ivy & Ocelot, EAB's Adult Learner Recruitment, CollegeVine's AI Recruiter and Apten. Mainstay is built for text-based nudging and student success coaching, and its evidence comes mostly from traditional-age students. Online programs often need more than that: phone calls, a text that turns into a live call, booked advisor appointments, warm transfers to enrollment coaches and write-back to a call-center CRM.


Most people searching "Mainstay alternatives" are coming up on a renewal. Mainstay itself also changed this year. In March 2026 the nonprofit Lemnis acquired Mainstay and is converting it into a nonprofit division, according to GovTech. A change of owner is a reasonable time to check whether the tool still fits the job.


This guide is fair to Mainstay, because it's good at what it was built for. Each competitor description below comes from that vendor's own website or from news coverage, as of October 2026. Apten is one of the vendors listed, and the section on when to stay with Mainstay says plainly when Mainstay is the better choice.


## What is Mainstay, and what is it good at?


Mainstay started as AdmitHub, a chatbot company for admissions offices. It now describes itself as an engagement platform that uses "behaviorally intelligent chatbots" to reach students by SMS, live chat, web chat and social media. Its homepage groups the product into three parts. AI Success Coaching gives each student a coach on their phone. Conversation Co-pilot helps staff, and Conversation Insights gives leaders a view of what students are asking at scale.


Mainstay's real strength is evidence. Its outcomes page cites a randomized controlled trial at Georgia State's Perimeter College, a 21.4% reduction in summer melt, and lower withdrawal rates tied to unpaid balances at Georgia State. Few vendors in this category have tested their messaging this carefully. It also integrates with Slate (two-way sync with custom field mapping) and with Ellucian Colleague, Banner and Recruit.


As of October 2026, GovTech reports that Mainstay's tools are used by more than 200 U.S. colleges and universities. We found no voice or phone-calling product on mainstay.com or in the acquisition coverage.


## Why do online and adult enrollment teams look for Mainstay alternatives?


Most of Mainstay's published wins are about first-year undergraduates: summer melt, FAFSA filing, fall registration and freshman yield. Those are real problems. They just aren't the problem a national online program with a call center has every Monday morning.


An online university's enrollment funnel looks more like a sales operation. RFIs arrive from paid search and lead vendors all day. Enrollment coaches are measured on contact rate, app starts and starts. The adult learner on the other end works full time, may prefer email, and often wants a real conversation about cost, transfer credit or clinical placements before applying. Here are the jobs that funnel needs covered:


-


**Instant first touch on every RFI.** In UPCEA's December 2025 secret shopper study, 44% of 1,000 inquiries to 182 institutions got no response at all, and the average reply took 14 hours and 23 minutes of business time. The fix is a reply in seconds, at any hour.


-


**Voice calls.** Many adult learners want to talk before they commit. An agent that only texts can answer questions, but it can't hold the conversation that gets a working parent to apply.


-


**Text to call.** The student replies by text, and the agent offers to call right now or at a time they pick. This is where a lot of applications actually start.


-


**Advisor booking and warm transfer.** When a student is ready, they should land on an enrollment coach's calendar or on the phone with one, and the coach should already have a summary.


-


**CRM write-back for the call center.** Many online programs run enrollment on Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics, not Slate. Coaches work from CRM views, so replies, opt-outs and qualification need to land on the record.


None of this means Mainstay is weak. It means the job is different. Warm transfers are covered in more depth in[AI handoff to admissions advisors](https://www.apten.ai/blog/ai-handoff-to-admissions-advisor-warm-transfer) , and the speed problem in[why college inquiries go unanswered](https://www.apten.ai/blog/college-inquiries-go-unanswered-speed-to-lead) .


## What are the best Mainstay alternatives in 2026?


Here are six vendors online and adult programs commonly evaluate against Mainstay. This isn't a ranking, and it isn't every vendor. Each row summarizes what the vendor's own site says as of October 2026. "Not described" means we couldn't find it on their public pages, not that it doesn't exist.


Vendor Channels (per vendor site) Voice calls CRM Best fit


Mainstay (baseline) SMS, live chat, web chat, social Not described Slate, Ellucian integrations Student success, retention and melt for traditional-age students


Element451 (Bolt agents) Chat, SMS, email, voice, WhatsApp Yes. Inbound calls with transfer to a forwarding number, and outbound calls per its help center Its own CRM, or on top of an existing one Schools open to an AI-native CRM, or wanting agents across admissions and student success


Mongoose (Cadence) Text, WhatsApp, web chat Not described Connectors, including Slate and Colleague Staff-run texting at scale. Student-facing AI agents listed as in development


Ivy & Ocelot (Gravyty) Chat, text, email, WhatsApp, social Gravyty sells a separate AI IVR for inbound calls Salesforce, Slate, Banner and others 24/7 question answering across admissions, aid and student services


EAB Adult Learner Recruitment Conversation Agent in email, landing pages and two-way SMS Not described Chat Agent syncs prospect data to your CRM Programs that want a partner to run lead generation and campaigns for them


CollegeVine AI Recruiter Phone, email, text, chat Yes, inbound inquiries by phone Uses data in your CRM (systems not named) Inbound coverage plus proactive outreach to defined populations


Apten SMS, voice, email, webchat, one shared memory Yes. Outbound and inbound, text to call, warm transfer Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot, Close High-volume online and adult programs with a call center of enrollment coaches


### Element451 (Bolt agents)


Element451 sells an AI-native higher ed CRM and Bolt, its AI agent platform. Its admissions agents page says Bolt agents "answer questions across chat, SMS, email, voice, and WhatsApp," and that they can run on Element's CRM or on top of the one you already have. Its help center describes inbound phone calls that transfer to one forwarding number per Element451 phone number, and outbound calls started by staff or run as campaigns through Bolt Jobs. If you're open to replacing your CRM, Element451 is the most complete single-vendor option here. If you're staying on Salesforce or Dynamics, ask how deep the write-back goes.


### Mongoose (Cadence)


Mongoose says more than 1,000 colleges and universities use it for two-way engagement over text, WhatsApp and web chat. Its AI today is staff-facing. Staff Assistant Agents such as the Inbox Assistant handle routine questions. Student-facing "Outcome Agents" are listed as in development. Mongoose fits teams that want humans in every conversation and a strong texting inbox. It doesn't describe voice calling.


### Ivy & Ocelot (Gravyty)


Ivy & Ocelot answers student questions 24/7 across chat, text, email, WhatsApp and social, and Gravyty says it can do proactive outreach to applicants. It lists integrations with Salesforce, Slate, Ellucian Banner and learning systems. Gravyty also sells a separate telephony product, an AI IVR that answers routine inbound calls. It's a good fit if your problem is question volume across many offices, not just admissions.


### EAB Adult Learner Recruitment


EAB's Adult Learner Recruitment is a fee-for-service partnership with a dedicated strategic leader. EAB builds the lead generation strategy and runs the multichannel campaigns. Its Conversation Agent can be embedded in outbound emails, landing pages and two-way SMS, and EAB's AI Chat Agent page says prospect data syncs to your CRM. This is a different buying decision from the others here. You're outsourcing part of the funnel, not licensing a tool your team runs.


### CollegeVine AI Recruiter


CollegeVine positions its AI Recruiter as a member of the enrollment team. It handles inbound inquiries over phone, email, text and chat, can go outbound to specific groups such as students who haven't filed the FAFSA, and personalizes emails from CRM data. Its public page doesn't describe warm transfer or appointment booking, so ask about both in a demo.


### Apten


Apten is a multichannel AI enrollment agent for online programs and large enrollment teams. It's covered in its own section below. The short version is one agent over SMS, voice, email and webchat that can move a student from text to a live call and warm-transfer them to an advisor, with write-back to Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot or Close.


Voice-only platforms are a separate category. They're compared in[the best AI voice agents for student enrollment](https://www.apten.ai/blog/best-ai-voice-agents-student-enrollment) , and the four product types are explained in[admissions chatbot vs AI enrollment agent](https://www.apten.ai/blog/admissions-chatbot-vs-ai-enrollment-agent) .


## When should you stay with Mainstay?


Switching costs time, and a renewal isn't a reason to churn on its own. Stay with Mainstay if most of these are true:


-


Your biggest goals are persistence, retention, summer melt or FAFSA completion, which is where Mainstay's research is strongest.


-


Your students are mostly traditional-age, and they respond well to text nudges.


-


Your CRM or SIS is Slate or Ellucian, and the sync works.


-


Your staff actually use the platform and trust the content libraries.


-


Phone conversations aren't central to how you enroll students.


Plenty of institutions keep Mainstay for student success and add a separate agent for top-of-funnel enrollment. That works, as long as the two don't text the same student about different things on the same day. Decide which system owns a student at each stage, and make sure opt-outs flow between them.


## How do you evaluate a Mainstay alternative?


Start from the gaps in your own funnel, not from feature lists. Pull these numbers from your CRM first:


1.


**Time to first reply on new RFIs, by hour of day.** If evenings and weekends are slow, you need instant automated replies, not a better inbox.


2.


**Share of RFIs that ever reach a live conversation.** If it's low, voice and text-to-call matter more than message volume.


3.


**What happens when a student asks for a person.** Trace five real cases. How long did each one wait, and did the advisor know the history?


4.


**What your coaches see in the CRM.** If replies and opt-outs from your texting tool don't show up in Salesforce or Dynamics, coaches call students who already said no.


Then run the same live tests with every vendor. Submit an RFI during the demo and time the reply. Text the agent, ask for a call, and listen for whether the call remembers the text. Ask for a warm transfer and then don't pick up, to see what the student gets. Ask which CRM fields change afterward and look at the record. A longer list of vendor questions is in[AI enrollment agent RFP questions](https://www.apten.ai/blog/ai-enrollment-agent-rfp-questions) .


Moving from texting to calling also adds TCPA obligations, including the AI-voice rules covered in[the 2026 AI compliance guide](https://www.apten.ai/blog/ai-compliance-guide-2026-tcpa-fcc-state-laws) . Ask whether one STOP shuts off every channel. This isn't legal advice, so run your outreach plan past counsel.


## How Apten handles online and adult enrollment


Apten runs one AI agent per student across SMS, voice, email and webchat, and it remembers everything said on every channel. When an RFI comes in, it replies within seconds, day or night. In Apten platform data (July 28 to October 25, 2026), the median school saw 53% of new inquiries reply to that first text within 24 hours.


The text thread is where many calls start. When a student is ready to talk, the agent can call them right away or schedule a call with reminder texts. About 1 in 4 students who reply by text move to a live call (Apten platform data, median 26%). If a call goes unanswered, the agent texts a follow-up, and voicemail detection keeps it from talking to an answering machine.


When a student wants a person, Apten warm-transfers them from a text, webchat or live call to an enrollment coach, with a summary. If no one picks up, it tries your fallback number if you've set one, texts the student the transfer number and can schedule a callback. It can also book appointments on Google Calendar or share a Calendly link, with a reminder before the meeting.


Apten writes mapped fields back to Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot or Close, including tags, a conversation summary, qualified, replied, transferred and opt-outs. Quiet hours follow the student's time zone, and STOP is honored per channel. Apten has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit and encrypts data at rest and in transit. We also help schools get A2P 10DLC registration approved. Consent capture and DNC scrubbing stay with your team.


## The bottom line


Mainstay is a well-researched tool for nudging traditional-age students through enrollment and keeping them enrolled. If your enrollment depends on reaching working adults fast, getting them on the phone and handing them to a coach who already knows their story, test the alternatives on those jobs. Use the same RFI, the same text-then-call test and the same CRM check with every vendor.
